Number the rows from top to bottom and columns from left to right. Reflection across diagonal \(\overline{BD}\) maps a square in position \((r,c)\) to \((5-c,5-r)\).

The black squares not already on the diagonal are:

\[
\begin{aligned}
(1,1)&\longleftrightarrow(4,4),\\
(1,3)&\longleftrightarrow(2,4),\\
(3,4)&\longleftrightarrow(1,2),\\
(4,2)&\longleftrightarrow(3,1).
\end{aligned}
\]

In each pair, the second square is currently white, so it must also be colored black. These are four distinct squares. The black square at \((1,4)\) lies on \(\overline{BD}\) and reflects onto itself, while all remaining white squares already have white reflection partners.

Therefore, coloring those four squares is both necessary and sufficient:

\[
\boxed{4}
\]
